name: maybe_Ui_PreloadTextId8
summary: Looks up UI text id 8 through the 2D manager (Ui_GetCore()->f_10) and discards the result; as the first vtable slot of its class, the effect is whatever the lookup itself does.
evidence: 32-byte body whose only action is the 0x00633560 lookup with the constant 8; 'preload' is inferred from the unused result, and the class vtable 0x00776E98 gives no further hint.

name: maybe_Ui_Fade_BeginSequence
summary: 36-byte wrapper that calls 0x002D24BC on the fade/transition manager (Ui_GetCore()->f_14), the same call the scripted-motion update makes when a motion ends.
evidence: Listed in the callback table at 0x00727300 together with 0x004C6ED0/0x004C754C/0x004C73C0; the callee 0x002D24BC is still unnamed, so 'begin fade sequence' remains the neighbourhood's reading.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_AdvanceWhenTransitioning
summary: Condition-table entry: when the screen manager is absent or its transition flag (+0x3D) is set, it jumps the caller's animator at self+0x48 to state 3; always returns 1.
evidence: The body reads the same manager flag as the named predicate 0x0059F928 but never returns it - it always returns 1 and drives the animator - so the old 'IsTransitioning' name (a predicate) was misleading; it is entry 0x727340 of the condition table next to 0x004C74AC.

name: Ui_UmaWindow_ApplyMode
signature: void Ui_UmaWindow_ApplyMode(UiUmaWindow* self, u8 mode, void* layout, int user)
summary: Applies the horse-race window mode: stores the mode byte at self+0x45C, copies it into the +0xBB byte of each of the five 0x70-byte entry rows, refreshes each row's text (UI string 0x15, or 0xF1 when the row's per-mode flag is set) and finally updates the root pane with the mode-dependent sprite.
evidence: Named callers maybe_Ui_UmaWindow_ToggleMode (0x004CC284) and Ui_UmaWindow_BuildModeRows (0x004CC670) both pass the new mode and rely on the five rows being re-labelled; the 5 x 0x70 row stride and the two string ids are explicit.

name: Ui_UmaWindow_Update
summary: Per-frame update: ticks the panel animation at self+0x98, advances the 1/30 s clock at +0x124/+0x128, fires the armed callback of entry self->f_120 (0x18-byte entries at self+0x11C) and clears the UI mode word when the +0x252 latch is set.
evidence: Same timer-pump template as the confirmed Svc_TimerSub_RunDue_24 (1/30 s literal 0x3D088889, 0x18-byte callback entries with +0x34/+0x38, 11-slot limit) and it is a slot of the horse-race window vtable 0x77A104.

name: maybe_Ui_Fade_PollEvent
summary: Polls the fade manager (Ui_GetCore()->f_14->f_1C) through virtual +0x14; when it reports an event it marks the panel dirty (+0x250 = 1) and, if the animator accepts state 10, applies it; always returns 1.
evidence: Companion of 0x004D9760 in the command table 0x0072B2C8; the fade-manager slot and the animator request/apply pair are visible, but no caller or string confirms the 'fade event' meaning.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_FillRewardRows
summary: Fills a two-column list: up to five value rows from the getter table at 0x0072CD60 (icon in column 0x3D, formatted number in 0x3E), then up to five item rows from the source list (item name/id below 0xC3 via Game_GetDataManager, quantity or flag text), blanking any unused rows.
evidence: The two five-row loops, the pane bases 0x3D/0x3E and the named Game_GetDataManager (0x0063E05C block) are explicit; 'reward' is still an inference from the item-id filtering, and the getter table itself is unnamed.

name: Ui_Screen_IsTransitionIdle
summary: Returns the inverse of the screen manager's transition flag (manager->f_3D ^ 1), or 0 when the manager does not exist.
evidence: The body is exactly 'flag ^ 1' on the same manager+0x98 object that 0x004C7508 tests, so the predicate and its polarity are proven; only the owner name ('screen') is inferred.

name: maybe_Script_GetSceneActiveObjectFlag
summary: Fetches the field singleton's scene and returns 0x632F80(scene), which is 1 when scene->f_10C exists and its +0x94 flag is set; Ghidra typed the stub void, so the return value is dropped in the readable C.
evidence: 36-byte leaf whose only work is the 0x632F80 query on scene f_10C; per the project's Ghidra rule a void stub that discards a getter result is the getter itself, so the old 'Check' name was wrong.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlayEffectAndSound
summary: Plays the gimmick's attached effect: when the field scene has an effect manager (scene->f_E8) it initialises the component at self+0xC0 and then submits the gimmick position (f_28/f_2C/f_30) through 0x002140E8.
evidence: The scene->f_E8 guard, the component init 0x003D55F4 and the three-float position submission are explicit; no caller and no sound API, so 'AndSound' is unsupported.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_ReleaseEffect
summary: Releases the gimmick's effect instance at self+0xEC back to the scene effect manager (scene->f_E8) through 0x003D55F4, without submitting a position.
evidence: Identical structure to 0x005D8460 with the other component offset (+0xEC vs +0xC0) and no position call, which is the release half of the pair; no caller.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateActionStateByCount
summary: When the scene is active and self->f_118 is below the incoming value, requests action-controller state 3 (0x006D3024 on self+0x34); always returns 1.
evidence: The guard func_00633070 (scene active) and the 'f_118 - compareValue < 0' test are visible, although Ghidra renders the borrow test as an unreadable SBORROW4 expression.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_StopStateMachine
summary: Calls virtual +0x1C with 0 on the object at Ui_GetCore()->f_14->f_10, i.e. stops/resets that controller; the function takes no other action.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x005DF260 and 0x005DB228 (same +0x1C(0) call on the same object) and has no caller, so only the call itself is known; 'gimmick state machine' is the neighbourhood's reading.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_EndActionWhenDone
summary: For event ids above 0x24, when the scene is active, asks the sub-controller at self+0x90 for state 3 and finishes it (virtual +0x10) when the request is accepted; always returns 1.
evidence: The event-id guard, the scene-active check 0x00633070 and the request/apply pair on self+0x90 are explicit; the 'end action' meaning comes from that pair, not from a named event table.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_StopStateMachineB
summary: Second copy of the 'stop the global gimmick controller' wrapper: calls virtual +0x1C with 0 on Ui_GetCore()->f_14->f_10 and nothing else.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x005D9EE0 and 0x005DF260; the separate address exists because a different callback-table slot points at it, so the suffix B is the only thing that distinguishes it.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_CopyPartAppearance
summary: Copies per-part appearance between two actors: matches the part ids in self->f_1C..f_20 against the actor's parts, then copies the u16 colour id and the +0x244 byte from the six-byte records at self->f_30..f_34 and requests controller state 1.
evidence: The body is damaged - unaff_r5 and in_r12 feed the copy, and Ghidra could not recover the jump table at 0x005DC770 - so only the part matching (0x00650D34) and the +0x242/+0x244 writes are trustworthy.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_SendOpenedEvent
summary: Builds and submits an interaction event: the record type becomes 3 when the gimmick id is 0x413, 4 when self->f_D2 is set, otherwise 2 with the id in the payload; it is then handed to the scene effect/event manager through 0x003D5648.
evidence: The three record types and the 0x413 special case are visible, and the submit callee 0x003D5648 is the sibling of the InitComponent* family used by the other gimmick handlers; 'opened' is inferred from the type split, not from a named event.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_IsEventIgnored
summary: Returns 0 when the event id is at least 0x10 and the field scene is active (the event is consumed), otherwise 1 (not handled, keep looking).
evidence: Only the event-id threshold and the scene-active check 0x00633070 are in the body, and the returned polarity is '1 = not handled' like the other action callbacks - so 'IsEventInputReady' described the opposite of what it returns.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_StopStateMachineC
summary: Third copy of the 'stop the global gimmick controller' wrapper (virtual +0x1C with 0).
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x005D9EE0 and 0x005DB228; no caller, so the suffix C only records that a third table slot points here.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_CheckToggleState
summary: Returns 0 when the scene is active and the door flag self->f_1D2 is clear; when the flag is set it requests controller state 3 (0x006D3CE8 on self+0x48) and returns 1; returns 1 unconditionally when the scene is inactive.
evidence: The f_1D2 flag and the state-3 request are explicit, and 0x005DF47C requests state 2 on the same controller, so the pair is a toggle; 'toggle state' is still a description, not a game term.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_SetToggleState
summary: When the scene is active, requests controller state 2 (0x006D3CE8 on self+0x48); always returns 1.
evidence: Single guarded call, paired with the state-3 request in 0x005DF434 on the same self+0x48 controller; the name only records the pairing.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_Callback005DFB14
summary: Unidentified gimmick callback: Ghidra emits only the Ui_GetCore fetch and then truncates with bad instruction data, so nothing about the body is known beyond its 192-byte size.
evidence: The readable body is two statements plus halt_baddata; the old 'UpdateTimerState' name asserted a timer state machine that the decompilation does not contain, so it was replaced by an address placeholder.

name: maybe_Ui_ReleaseGpuBuffer
summary: Releases the widget's buffer at self+0x20 through the UI object releaser when the flag bits 0x24 are set in self+0x18, and clears the pointer.
evidence: The guarded release+clear is explicit and 0x0021F8B8 is the shared UI-object releaser; whether the buffer is a GPU buffer is still an inference from the 0x0062xxxx block.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_ReleaseGpuBufferEx
summary: Extended buffer release: installs the vtable, releases the buffer at self+0x20, clears the global owner pointer 0x007A9AE8, marks the render object's +0xB6 byte as 2 and unregisters the embedded list node.
evidence: The body is truncated after the 0x0036B514 node removal (halt_baddata) and the render-object access is garbled, so the extra steps are only partly verifiable; the shared buffer offset with 0x00621EC0 is what ties it to the same release path.

name: maybe_Ui_QueryTransitionBusyInState7
summary: Returns the 2D manager's transition-busy flag (Ui_GetCore()->f_14->f_C virtual +0x18) but only while the caller object is in state 7, otherwise 0.
evidence: Identical shape to the corrected 0x00630898 (same manager slot +0x18 query) with the guard self->f_578 == 7; the old 'MessageConditionCheck' name claimed a script/message meaning the body does not show.

name: maybe_Ui_GetTransitionFlag
summary: Returns the screen manager's transition flag byte (manager+0x98, f_3D), or 1 when the manager does not exist.
evidence: The byte it returns is exactly the flag that Ui_Screen_IsTransitionIdle (0x0059F928) inverts and that 0x004C7508 tests; nothing in the body reads a text-speed setting, so the old 'GetTextSpeed' name was wrong.

name: maybe_Ui_QueryTransitionBusyB
summary: Returns the 2D manager's transition-busy flag (Ui_GetCore()->f_14->f_C virtual +0x18) when the object's f_11C field is set (-1 means 'no entry'), otherwise 0.
evidence: Same manager slot +0x18 query as the corrected 0x00630898, only the guard field differs (f_11C instead of f_C); the named caller maybe_Ui_DiveResultWindow_Update (0x0032C33C) uses it as a 'wait for the transition' condition.

name: maybe_Ui_QueryTransitionBusyInState1A
summary: Returns the 2D manager's transition-busy flag but only while the caller object's f_578 state byte equals 0x1A, otherwise 0.
evidence: Guard self->f_578 == 0x1A plus the same manager +0x18 query as 0x00630898/0x006410F4; the old 'MessageConditionCheck' name claimed a message meaning that is not in the body.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_IsTransitionBusy_State4A8
summary: True only while the window's f_4A8 mode byte is set and the 2D manager reports a pending transition through virtual +0x18.
evidence: Named caller maybe_Ui_StatusWindow_UpdateState (0x00295790) uses the result to hold the state machine back, and the manager query is the same one the confirmed Ui_MessageWindow_IsTransitionBusy uses; only the f_4A8 guard is specific to this window class.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_IsTransitionBusy_State12
summary: Same transition-busy test as 0x0063BEFC but gated on the window state byte f_578 == 0x12.
evidence: Guard f_578 == 0x12 plus the manager +0x18 query; the sibling 0x00641574 does the same for state 0x13, so the family is established but no caller exists.

name: Ui_IsWindowReady
summary: Returns true when no message window is open, or when the open window has both readiness bytes f_3D and f_3E set; false while a window is still opening.
evidence: The three-way test (no window / flag f_3D / flag f_3E) is explicit and the same core->f_10->f_98 window object with those flags is used by the message-window code at 0x001993C4; no caller (vtable slot).

name: Script_FormatValues
summary: Implementation of the script string-format native: reads the value at VM slot 2 (and the format string at slot 3 when more than two arguments were passed, defaulting to 'unnamedbuffer'), runs the VM format routine and returns 1, or -1 when it fails.
evidence: The named VM accessors Script_Vm_GetString/Script_Vm_GetType and the 'unnamedbuffer' default literal at 0x0015709C make the argument layout explicit; the same 0x006BB570 format entry is called with (vm, buffer, type, format, 0).

name: Field_Gadget_SetState
summary: Applies a state to the field gadget selected by the gadget list: resolves the gadget through Field_GadgetList_FindOrAddBySlotId, follows its handle to the model object and either releases the state part (mode 0) or creates the state effects (any other mode).
evidence: Both callees are now named (Model_ReleaseStatePart 0x002318B0 and Model_CreateStateEffects 0x0022FA0C) and the two branches differ only by mode, which fixes the set/clear meaning; the gadget lookup and handle walk are explicit.

name: Ui_Menu_DeactivatePage
summary: Deactivates one page: resolves the window's model object through its handle, releases that page's state effect (Model_ReleaseStatePart) and clears the page's bit in the global enabled-element mask at work+0x2A628.
evidence: The named callee Model_ReleaseStatePart and the bit-clear 'mask[page>>5] &= ~(1 << (page & 0x1F))' are explicit, and the named caller PlayerSetFieldEffect (0x0015A524) passes the page id; it is the exact mirror of the activate path 0x0023CAA8.

name: Ui_Menu_ClearMode
summary: Leaves the special display mode: clears the two mode bytes at work+0x2D549 and work+0x2D54A, releases the page-1 state effect of the window's model object and clears bit 1 of the global enabled-element mask.
evidence: The two byte clears, the named Model_ReleaseStatePart(obj, 1) and the '&= ~2' mask clear are explicit, and the named caller maybe_Ui_Menu_EnsureDisplayState (0x003F18F8) uses it to undo the mode it set.
